LoloBuy return and refund guide: check before shipping

A return is easiest to assess while the item is still in China. Use the order status, seller terms, warehouse condition and evidence together before expecting a cancellation, refund or exchange.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s public order-return, cancellation, warehouse inspection and parcel after-sales materials, checked on 28 September 2026. Seller decisions and live platform rules control each case; confirm the current order page before acting.

Start with the question: where is the item?

The useful starting point for a LoloBuy return and refund guide is not “Do they accept returns?” It is “Where is the item right now?” A request made before purchase, a product already bought from a third-party seller, an item stored in LoloBuy’s warehouse and a parcel delivered overseas are four different situations.

LoloBuy provides a shopping-agent workflow for products sold by third parties. That means seller rules and seller approval can determine whether a product return succeeds. Once an item has entered international shipping, sending the product back to the original seller is no longer the same task as using parcel after-sales for loss, damage or a wrong item.

Open the exact record in “My LoloBuy” and write down the order or parcel number, current status, the time that status began and the remedy you want. Do this before contacting support. A precise request is easier to investigate than a message that mixes an order cancellation, warehouse return and international delivery complaint.

Before purchase: screen the return risk

The cheapest return is the one you avoid needing. Save the product link, selected colour, size, version, quantity and any seller note before paying. Check whether the listing identifies the item as used, customized, clearance, final sale or otherwise ineligible for ordinary returns. LoloBuy’s public guidance says used-product and warehouse-sale orders do not support product returns.

Do not treat a marketplace badge as a platform guarantee. LoloBuy’s help material describes a limited return or exchange window for eligible third-party listings, but it also says the product must remain new and meet the seller’s resale requirements. Packaging, tags, accessories and seals can therefore affect whether the seller accepts it.

For manual-order or special-platform products, risk can be higher. The live product-entry disclaimer says some third-party channels may not provide the same return or exchange service as ordinary marketplace listings. If the return terms are unclear, resolve that uncertainty before purchase rather than assuming support can reverse the transaction later.

Match the request to the order status

The official cancellation guide separates early order stages from later return stages. Use the live wording in your account, because labels can change, but the practical logic is consistent:

  • Awaiting payment: no paid refund should be necessary; remove or leave the unpaid order according to the available controls.
  • Not processed or under review: a paid order may still be cancellable before sourcing work begins.
  • Processing: submit cancellation immediately. The buyer cannot safely assume the seller has not yet been paid.
  • Purchased or ordered: the shopping agent must ask the seller to cancel or refund. Approval is no longer solely a platform action.
  • Shipped domestically or arriving at the warehouse: wait for the item to be recorded as stored, then use the return or exchange action if the listing and condition qualify.
  • Stored: treat the displayed warehouse deadline as urgent. Do not wait until parcel submission to reconsider the item.

LoloBuy’s current return page says eligible stored items should be submitted for return or exchange within five days after the storage date. A related guarantee page describes this as 120 hours beginning after stock-in. Because platform interfaces and seller rules can change, use the deadline shown on the live order record and submit earlier when possible.

What makes a warehouse return eligible?

A visible return button does not guarantee approval. Check four things before relying on it:

  1. Listing eligibility: does the original product page support unconditional returns or exchanges?
  2. Time: is the order still inside the live warehouse application window?
  3. Condition: can the item be returned without affecting the seller’s ability to resell it?
  4. Seller decision: has the seller agreed to accept the return or exchange?

If the item has no verified quality problem, LoloBuy’s published terms say the buyer may be responsible for delivery costs between seller and warehouse and a return or exchange service charge. “Free shipping” on the original listing does not necessarily make the reverse journey free. The guidance explains that the seller may have paid the outbound domestic cost and may recover it when the order is returned.

Keep enough account balance to cover any displayed return costs. Read the calculated charges before confirming. A low-value item may be technically returnable but uneconomic to send back once two-way domestic shipping and service costs are included.

Use QC evidence for the right kind of claim

A preference change and a seller fault are different claims. If you simply chose the wrong size or no longer want the colour, describe that honestly. If the item is wrong, visibly damaged or materially different from the saved selection, point to the exact mismatch.

LoloBuy’s standard warehouse inspection focuses on visible information such as style, quantity, colour, size and model. Sealed goods are generally not opened, and professional electronics, authenticity, functionality and performance fall outside the normal inspection scope. A missing functional test is therefore not proof that the warehouse overlooked a defect.

Build a compact evidence set before filing:

  • order number and seller listing;
  • saved option or order screenshot;
  • the clearest QC photo showing the issue;
  • a close-up plus a full-item view;
  • size label or model marking when relevant;
  • one sentence stating the requested remedy.

Avoid vague claims such as “quality bad.” Say, for example, that the ordered option was size M while the photographed label shows size L, or that the listing specified two units while the warehouse record shows one. Evidence should make the mismatch understandable without guessing.

Understand what “refund” means in the workflow

A seller agreeing to a return is not the same event as money appearing immediately. The item may need to travel back, be received by the seller and pass the seller’s check before funds are released. LoloBuy’s current page says accepted refunds are credited to the user’s available LoloBuy balance and that later-stage refunds depend on the seller.

Published time ranges are estimates for specific statuses, not universal promises. The clock can depend on whether the purchase was already completed, whether domestic return shipping is required and how quickly the seller confirms receipt. Track the return parcel number when one is supplied and keep the order open until both the seller decision and balance movement are recorded.

Also separate the product amount from incidental costs. A successful product refund does not automatically prove that domestic freight, return freight, service charges, payment conversion differences or international shipping will be reimbursed. Ask which amount was approved and where it will be credited.

After international dispatch: use parcel after-sales

Once the parcel has left for another country, the warehouse return window is no longer the correct route. For a wrong, damaged or missing item discovered after delivery, LoloBuy’s public instructions direct users to “My LoloBuy” → “Parcels” → “Apply After-sales” for the corresponding parcel.

Act promptly and follow the deadline displayed on the current parcel record. LoloBuy’s public pages contain different timing statements for different after-sales circumstances, so there is no safe reason to wait. Preserve the outer parcel, label, seals, internal packaging and all contents until the case is reviewed.

For visible transit damage, photograph the unopened parcel from multiple angles before removing items. For a missing item, photograph the parcel label, contents, packing list if present and the package on a scale before discarding packaging. For the wrong product, show the full item, its identifying label and the ordered specification. If the courier allows damage remarks or refusal at delivery, follow its current procedure without making a false statement.

A risk-based decision checklist

Cancel now when the order is still in an early stage and the account provides cancellation. Waiting can turn a platform-side cancellation into a seller negotiation.

Request a warehouse return when the item is stored, the seller terms allow it, the deadline is open, the condition meets resale requirements and the expected refund justifies the costs.

Ask a precise question when eligibility, responsibility or cost is unclear. Request confirmation of the seller rule, application deadline, estimated deductions and evidence needed before you authorize anything.

Use parcel after-sales when the item has already shipped internationally and the problem concerns delivery, damage, shortage or the wrong contents. Attach evidence from the parcel, not only the original listing.

Do not ship yet when QC shows an unresolved mismatch. International dispatch usually makes a seller-stage remedy slower, costlier or impractical.

Conclusion: return decisions are stage decisions

The practical lesson from this LoloBuy return and refund guide is simple: identify the stage before choosing the remedy. Check seller eligibility before purchase, use QC while the item is still in China, respect the warehouse deadline, calculate return costs and preserve parcel evidence after delivery. The earlier the problem is documented, the more clearly you can separate a change of mind from a seller error or shipping issue.
